article_title: 翻转的逻辑：大脑睡眠-清醒

sources.authors: Kroeger D, Bandaru SS, Madara JC, Saper CB
sources.title: Galanin neurons in the ventrolateral preoptic area promote sleep and heat loss in mice
key_findings: VLPO-galanin neurons constitute ~85% of sleep-active neurons in VLPO
Low-frequency optogenetic stimulation (1-4 Hz) increases NREM sleep by >60%
High-frequency stimulation (>8 Hz) causes wakefulness via depolarization block
Chemogenetic activation induces profound hypothermia (4-6°C within ~2 hours)
VLPO-Gal neurons project to TMN, LC, LH, parabrachial, PPT

sources.title: The Interaction Between the Ventrolateral Preoptic Nucleus and the Tuberomammillary Nucleus in Regulating the Sleep-Wakefulness Cycle
key_findings: VLPO L-glutamate injection → NREM +56.4%, wakefulness -21.6%
TMN L-glutamate injection → wakefulness +35%, sleep -35.2%
GABA-A blockade in TMN reverses VLPO-induced sleep
H1 receptor blockade in VLPO reduces TMN-induced wakefulness by 30.2%
Confirms VLPO→GABA→TMN and TMN→His(H1)→VLPO mutual inhibition circuit

sources.authors: Williams RH, Jensen LT, Verkhratsky A, Fugger L, Burdakov D, Scammell TE
sources.title: Optogenetic-mediated release of histamine reveals distal and autoregulatory mechanisms for controlling arousal
key_findings: Optogenetic TMN activation decreases inhibitory inputs to TMN (disinhibition)
Histamine suppresses VLPO via H1 receptors through interneurons (indirect)
H3 autoreceptors provide negative feedback on histamine release
Supports the flip-flop model with optogenetic causal evidence

sources.authors: Fulcher BD, Phillips AJK, Postnova S, Robinson PA
sources.title: A physiologically based model of orexinergic stabilization of sleep and wake
key_findings: Orexin stabilizes wakefulness by raising the barrier against inadvertent sleep transitions
Without orexin: bistable region with low transition thresholds → narcolepsy-like fragmentation
Orexin also relays circadian input to monoaminergic nuclei
Model predicts preserved total sleep duration with orexin loss (consistent with NT1)

sources.authors: Li SB, Damonte VM, Chen C, Wang GX, Bhatt K, Bhatt D, et al. (de Lecea L)
sources.title: Hyperexcitable arousal circuits drive sleep instability during aging
key_findings: Aged mice: orexin neurons more frequently active during sleep (hyperexcitable)
Molecular mechanism: reduced KCNQ2 expression → impaired M-current → hyperexcitability
Kcnq2/3 knockout in young mice replicates aging sleep fragmentation phenotype
Flupirtine (KCNQ2/3 activator) restores sleep quality in aged mice
Age-related KCNQ2 downregulation linked to epigenetic changes
used_in_article_sections: 新发现：老年性睡眠碎片化的分子机制

sources.authors: Tyree SM, Borniger JC, de Lecea L
sources.title: Hypocretin as a Hub for Arousal and Motivation
key_findings: Orexin integrates metabolic (glucose, leptin, ghrelin), stress (amygdala), and reward (NAc) signals
Projects to LC (NE), TMN (His), VTA (DA), DR (5-HT), PVN (stress)
Hunger→orexin→arousal pathway for food-seeking behavior
Stress-induced insomnia: amygdala→orexin→suppresses VLPO

sources.title: The neural circuit of orexin (hypocretin): maintaining sleep and wakefulness
key_findings_from_abstract: Orexin regulates sleep-wake cycles through interactions with emotion, reward, and energy homeostasis systems

sources.authors: Bassetti CLA, Adamantidis A, Burdakov D, et al.
sources.title: Narcolepsy—clinical spectrum, aetiopathophysiology, diagnosis and treatment
key_findings_from_abstract: Narcolepsy type 1: selective loss of ~70,000 orexin neurons in lateral hypothalamus
Diagnostic: CSF orexin-A < 110 pg/mL; HLA-DQB1*06:02 positive
Symptoms: EDS, cataplexy, hallucinations, sleep paralysis

sources.authors: Saper CB, Cano G, Scammell TE
sources.title: Homeostatic, circadian, and emotional regulation of sleep
key_findings_from_abstract: VLPO inhibits arousal regions; reciprocally inhibited by them → flip-flop model
Orexin neurons stabilize sleep-wake transitions; narcolepsy results from their absence

sources.authors: Venner A, Todd WD, Fraigne J, Bowman C, Bhatt D, Bhatt K, et al. (Fuller PM)
sources.title: An Inhibitory Lateral Hypothalamic-Preoptic Circuit Mediates Rapid Arousals from Sleep
key_findings_from_abstract: LH GABAergic neurons → directly inhibit VLPO sleep-promoting neurons
Circuit receives input from stress and arousal-related brain regions
First demonstration that direct synaptic inhibition of VLPO suppresses sleep neurons

sources.title: A quantitative model of sleep-wake dynamics based on the physiology of the brainstem ascending arousal system
key_findings_from_abstract: Mathematical model shows flip-flop behavior from VLPO-MA mutual inhibition
Bistable regions in drive space with stable wake and sleep states
Narcolepsy simulation: reduced inhibition → increased state transitions
used_in_article_sections: 机制一（触发器的物理学）

sources.authors: Sun Y, Tisdale RK, Kilduff TS
sources.title: Hypocretin/Orexin Receptor Pharmacology and Sleep Phases
key_findings: OX1R (HCRTR1): motivation, reward, and autonomic functions
OX2R (HCRTR2): strongly linked to sleep-wake control
FDA-approved orexin receptor antagonists: suvorexant (2014), lemborexant (2019)

summary.quality_note: Strong causal evidence for VLPO-TMN mutual inhibition (optogenetics). Orexin-as-stabilizer supported by mathematical modeling and narcolepsy genetics/clinical data. Most direct experiments in rodents; human translation via clinical narcolepsy data.
